name: Emerging-market stress
summary: Rupiah holds near record lows around 18,200/$ after Bank Indonesia's rate rise; no EM default or IMF rescue found
state: The rupiah weakened past 18,200 per dollar on 24 Nov after touching a record low of 18,300 on 19 Nov; it is down about 9% this year, and Bank Indonesia has raised rates by 125bp since May to 6% (Trading Economics). The rupiah's fall has been gradual, short of 10% in a month. No major emerging economy in default, imposing capital controls or seeking emergency IMF support was found as of 25 Nov, so the level stays Normal.
for_you: Travellers and importers dealing in Indonesian rupiah face a weak currency. Wider emerging-market debt markets show no acute distress.
rubric_hit: Normal: no major EM currency down >10% in a month, no default or emergency IMF request

sources.title: Trading Economics — Rupiah Slips on Dollar Strength, Domestic Caution

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
